government.note: Unrecognised de facto state that is de jure part of Moldova. The directly elected President (Igor Smirnov from 1991) headed both state and government in 2000; a Vice President existed until 2011. Amendments of June 2011 created the post of Prime Minister (Chairman of the Government), appointed by the President, from 1 January 2012 (first holder from 18 January 2012). The Supreme Council elected in 1995 was bicameral (67 deputies); amendments in 2000 made it a unicameral body of 43 deputies, reduced to 33 from 2020.

holders.vacant_reason: The office did not exist from 9 December 1990 until it was re-established under the June 2011 constitutional amendments; the President headed the government.
Stanislav Kasap (born 1983) was acting Prime Minister; he has no Wikidata item and is not recorded as a person.

system.note: Single-member constituencies, first past the post. On 1 January 2000 the Supreme Council elected in 1995 had 67 deputies in two chambers (32 in the Chamber of Legislators, 35 in the Chamber of Representatives); from the December 2000 election it was unicameral with 43 seats, and 33 seats from 2020. The seat count here is the 2000 size because seats_2000 must match it.

chambers.review_note: The party composition of the 1995-2000 Supreme Council was not found (there is no English Wikipedia article on the 1995 election); all 67 seats are recorded as 'others'. The chamber size also changed to 43 (December 2000) and 33 (2020), which the schema cannot express.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Estimate for a de facto state without party-list voting. Anchored on Igor Smirnov's 71.9% in the 1996 presidential election (statist, pro-presidential camp) and the predominance of independents in the Supreme Council; the remainder is spread across communist, business-oriented and other groups.
